title: Cyrenaica
capsule: Cyrenaica was the ancient Greek colonial region of northeastern Libya, centred on the five cities (Pentapolis) of Cyrene, Apollonia, Barce, Teucheira, and Euesperides. Cyrene was founded c. 631 BC by Dorian colonists from Thera; Alexander the Great received the region's voluntary surrender in 331 BC, and it passed to the Ptolemaic dynasty before being bequeathed to Rome by Ptolemy Apion in 96 BC and constituted as a senatorial province (with Crete) in 74 BC. The region was agriculturally rich — its silphium plant was a luxury export prized across the Mediterranean — and philosophically notable as the home of the Cyrenaic school of Aristippus. A major Jewish revolt under the messianic claimant Lukuas (115–117 AD) devastated Cyrene's population and infrastructure.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Pentapolis territory is archaeologically and textually well-attested; the southern hinterland boundary in the Sahara is undefined in ancient sources, and the geometric window (-331 to -91) captures the Ptolemaic-controlled phase specifically.
